summary: Trail Cons. - Conversation with the Artist | Eastside Family Garden Project
location: Lorraine “Grandma” Camacho Activity Center, 35 Robert T Martinez Jr St, Austin, TX 78702
description:
Join The Trail Conservancy for a Meet the Artist event for the Eastside Play Area project! Talk with the project’s artist, Lys Santamaria and landscape architect, Rialto Studio. Together, we’ll explore how community stories and creativity can shape the art that makes our park a true reflection of home.
Free Tacos and Beverages will be provided.
Get to Know the Artist: Lys Santamaria
Selected from an open call in July, Lys is a Colombian-born, Austin-based artist whose work in glass beads and tile explores joy, healing, and storytelling inspired by her identity as a Latina, woman, and immigrant.
As a public artist, Lys describes her role as “a translator”—listening to communities, honoring their stories, and reflecting them through intentional design. Her current projects include a commission for the Joan Means Khabele Bathhouse Rehabilitation.

summary: Trail Cons. - Wishbone Bridge Ribbon Cutting Celebration
description:
Wishbone Bridge & Unity Underpass Ribbon Cutting Celebration
The completion of the Wishbone Bridge marks a milestone for the Butler Trail, completing the 10-mile loop and creating a seamless, traffic-free experience for Trail users! Join The Trail Conservancy and the City of Austin on Saturday, February 7th, from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. for a celebration and party on the plaza and be one of the first to enjoy the new pedestrian bridge, underpass, and benches.
RSVP: https://secure.qgiv.com/for/thetrailconservancy/event/wishboneribboncutting/
Getting There
There are three entrances to the Wishbone Bridge:
- South of Longhorn Dam (entrance to the Unity Underpass)
- North of Longhorn Dam at the end of Canterbury St.
- North of the Longhorn Dam at the end of the old Holly peninsula

summary: Trail Cons. - Merlin Tuttle Day: Congress Ave. Bat Celebration
location: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bat Bridge, 100 S Congress Ave, Austin, TX 78704
description:
Merlin Tuttle Day: Congress Ave Bat Celebration
Thanks to renowned bat conservationist Merlin Tuttle’s lifelong dedication, bats are now a staple of Austin’s culture. Former Austin Mayor Steve Adler officially proclaimed Merlin’s birthday, August 26th, as Merlin Tuttle Day in honor of Merlin’s success in saving the city’s now world-famous bats. And this year, we’re celebrating the addition of a new, more interactive visitor experience on the Trail: Bat City.

summary: Trail Cons. - Open House: Eastside Family Garden Design Concepts
location: Lorraine “Grandma” Camacho Activity Center, 35 Robert T Martinez Jr St, Austin, TX 78702
description:
Eastside Family Garden Project Open House
See the future of the Trail’s Eastside! Join The Trail Conservancy at the Camacho Activity Center to see the latest design and art concepts for the Eastside Family Garden project!
- Breakfast tacos provided
- Meet Lys Santamaria (project artist consultant) and Edith Uresti from Rialto Studio (project landscape architect) and learn about the artistic interpretation in the project
- See the latest project designs and art concepts
About the Project
The Eastside Family Garden will revitalize over 2 acres of neglected parkland, creating a recreational space that blends traditional playscapes, nature play, and inviting gathering areas—all purposefully designed with shade, native restoration, and water access in mind.

summary: Trail Cons. - Open House: Programming for the Butler Trail and Seaholm Waterfront
location: Seaholm Intake Facility, 801 West Cesar Chavez Street, Austin, TX 78701
description:
New community engagement focuses exclusively on shaping future public programming for the Butler Trail and the future Seaholm Waterfront, and we invite community input to guide activities that are engaging, educational, and uniquely Austin.
The Seaholm Intake Building (801 W Cesar Chavez St) is an iconic, historic building set right on the Trail that offers a world of possibility. In partnership with the Austin Parks and Recreation Department, The Trail Conservancy will undertake a renovation of this building and its grounds to create Seaholm Waterfront, a unique space for everyone who lives, works, and travels in Austin. Phase 2 renovations could include a cafe, overhead doors, a front porch, indoor restrooms, a lake overlook, a front lawn, seating areas, and planting areas.
